title: Fufu Pounding Rhythm
summary: Fufu is a smooth dough of pounded cassava, yam or plantain, made in a large wooden mortar across Ghana, Nigeria and neighbouring countries. Two cooks share the work: one swings the pestle while the other turns and wets the dough between strokes, and the labour settles into a steady beat.
howToPlay: Three pads stand for the mortar: the heavy pound, the partner's pound and the quick turn of the dough.
Notes travel toward a line at the bottom; strike the pad just as its note arrives.
Keep time with the steady pounding, then quicken to the two pestles and finish on the three-beat figure.
The turn always falls in the gap between pounds, so keep your hand clear of the pestle.
rules: The pound is the deep stroke and the partner's pound is a lighter answer; the turn is a short quick stroke between them.
A stroke within a hair of the note is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while a song is running costs a few points.
Each song plays twice; three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
Two songs run in four beats to the bar and one in three.
heritageNote: Pounding fufu is everyday household work in West and Central Africa, often done by two people or more, and the sound of the pestles carries across a compound at mealtime. The skill of keeping the beat and turning the dough without a mistake is learned from watching family.
